named_question: When does an ordinary SID32..90 edit clear CID, and how can the CLI require explicit acceptance without changing occupied/no-op branches?

static_byte_pins.purpose: Unoccupied requested1..90 branch checks selected CID>0 and requested>=32, asks Yes/No, skips transaction on No7 and otherwise stores CID0 before ordered SID transaction.
Constructor zero initialization at+0xa8 includes CID; omitted CID default0 is already bound by the reused reader contract.

reused_contracts.fact: Reuse owner ordinary-ID mapping, exact row/identity selection, occupancy, explicit occupied-ID exchange and ordered temporary99 ScMv remaps. Its earlier1..31 CLI subset is historical.
Omitted CID reads0; reuse existing selection_plan codec and independent CID identity result conventions.

source_contract.range: The unoccupied branch explicitly accepts requested1..90. Owner mapping preserves ordinary values; special776/777/778 conversion remains outside CLI scope.
source_contract.clear: Only unoccupied requested>=32 with selected CID>0 asks the CID-clear confirmation. Accepting Yes clears selected CID to0 then enters the same SID/reference transaction. CLI does not simulate dialog errors or incidental refresh effects.
source_contract.not_clear: Requested<=31, numeric no-op and occupied exchange bypass this free-higher-ID clear branch. In particular occupied higher-ID exchange does not clear CID; it asks its separate swap confirmation.
source_contract.atomicity: Native clear precedes remapping, but CLI plans and validates every needed identity/reference before applying either change, so unsupported input never leaves a half-cleared CID.

CLI_policy.command: lox config lighting set-mood-sid FILE BLOCK --mood SID_OR_NAME --sid 1..90 [--swap] [--allow-cid-clear]
CLI_policy.eligibility: Selected/requested ordinary1..90; retain exact direct selection, matching Num, all positive numerically unique signed32 direct SIDs and temporary99 occupied-swap collision guard.
CLI_policy.confirmation: Free requested32..90 with positive selected CID requires --allow-cid-clear. The flag is permission for that recovered branch, not an unconditional CID clear, and does not grant --swap.
CLI_policy.needed_CID: Only the free changed higher-ID branch parses selected CID. Support nonnegative signed32 or omission (effective0), reject unsupported explicit storage. Missing/+000 zero is retained without inserting/canonicalizing CID0. Other branches preserve even unneeded opaque CID spelling.
CLI_policy.effects: Change affected SIDs, accepted selected CID0 and needed ordered ScMv only. No CID clearing on occupied/no-op/lower branches, no other CID, IID, Qn, flags, names, count/width/order, HCL, capabilities, sequences, OpM/ScAc or unknown data changed.
CLI_policy.result: JSON adds cid_cleared for the actual effect; existing identity/selection CSV rows show before/after CID. Existing four-argument Rust entry remains a default-no-clear wrapper.
